lines: A drum voice that synthesises a flatulence sound from a low tanh-shaped sine, brown and pink noise, and randomly fired bubble, formant and hiss events
Lowers the pitch of the tone, over 0 to 100; the core sine runs at 120Hz at the bottom of the travel and 50Hz at the top
Sets the attack, the decay and the peak of the envelope, over 0 to 1; at the top the attack is 80ms and the decay half a second, at the bottom 230ms and 1 second
Sets how far the slow pitch wobble and the random pitch drift reach, over 0 to 1; it also slows the fall of the pressure envelope and lengthens the formant ring
Lowers the whole output, over 0 to 1, by the square of what is left; at the top the module is silent
Sets the level of the noise layer and the loudness of the hiss bursts, over 0 to 1
Sets how wet the sound is, over 0 to 1: it moves the noise from brown toward pink, raises the resonant overtone, and makes the bubble and hiss events more frequent and louder
Restarts the envelope from the beginning when it is pressed, and holds the pressure envelope up for as long as it is held
Takes the Age knob over: -10V to 10V is spread across that knob's whole travel, and the knob cannot be set by hand while a cable is patched here
Takes the Urgency knob over: -10V to 10V is spread across that knob's whole travel, and the knob cannot be set by hand while a cable is patched here
Takes the Retention knob over: -10V to 10V is spread across that knob's whole travel, and the knob cannot be set by hand while a cable is patched here
Takes the Shame knob over: -10V to 10V is spread across that knob's whole travel, and the knob cannot be set by hand while a cable is patched here
Takes the Surprise knob over: -10V to 10V is spread across that knob's whole travel, and the knob cannot be set by hand while a cable is patched here
Takes the Food knob over: -10V to 10V is spread across that knob's whole travel, and the knob cannot be set by hand while a cable is patched here
Restarts the envelope on each rise above 1V, and holds the pressure envelope up for as long as the voltage stays there
The finished sound, soft-clipped through a tanh to about ±5.2V
Note — Every CV input writes into the knob it belongs to rather than adding to it, so the knob moves on screen while a cable is patched and keeps the position the cable left it in.
Note — The module makes one sound as soon as it is placed in the rack: the envelope starts from the beginning with no trigger needed.
Note — The six knobs are read once every 64 samples, so modulation faster than that arrives in steps.
Note — An eighth input is declared and read alongside the trigger, with no jack drawn on the panel, so nothing can ever be patched into it.

0.why: module.hpp:242-246 maps the voltage onto 0 to 100 and writes it into the Age parameter with setDisplayValue; the CV term computed on line 246 is then always 0

1.why: module.hpp:249-253 maps the voltage onto 0 to 1 and writes it into the Urgency parameter with setDisplayValue; the CV term computed on line 253 is then always 0

2.why: module.hpp:256-260 maps the voltage onto 0 to 1 and writes it into the Retention parameter with setDisplayValue; the CV term computed on line 260 is then always 0

3.why: module.hpp:263-267 maps the voltage onto 0 to 1 and writes it into the Shame parameter with setDisplayValue; the CV term computed on line 267 is then always 0

4.why: module.hpp:270-274 maps the voltage onto 0 to 1 and writes it into the Surprise parameter with setDisplayValue; the CV term computed on line 274 is then always 0

5.why: module.hpp:277-281 maps the voltage onto 0 to 1 and writes it into the Food parameter with setDisplayValue; the CV term computed on line 281 is then always 0

6.why: module.hpp:131-138 tests getVoltage() > 1.f and resets the envelope only on the rise, with no channel read

0.why: module.hpp:227-228 passes the mix through fastTanh, which is bounded to 1, and multiplies by 5.2 before setVoltage; setChannels is never called

FartSynthson.notes: Source read at commit 5c6f38d. Every one of the nineteen commits says version 2.0.0, so the installed art settled it: res/layout.svg matches only the last three commits (6f28461, eeaa2ec, 5c6f38d), and the differences between those three are an include, the spelling of pi and a Makefile flag, so all three behave alike. The six CV inputs are not summed with their knobs: module.hpp:242-283 calls setDisplayValue on the parameter and then subtracts the parameter's new value from the same figure, so the offset added in process is always zero and the CV works only by moving the knob, which it also saves into the patch. BUTTON_INPUT, input index 7, is read at module.hpp:133 but was never given a configInput or a PortWidget, so it has no name and no jack. The button carries no printed name on the panel; the maker's tooltip calls it Let it out.
